name: Hanzomon
tagline: Otemachi in 8 minutes and Shibuya in 11 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 8 minutes to Otemachi, 17 minutes to Shinjuku, 11 minutes to Shibuya and 25 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 29.4 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 20.8 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 29.4 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 10 m to 30.8 m, a difference of 20.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 11 clinics and 15 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 茂恵会半蔵門病院, about 2 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 友仁会赤坂見附前田病院, about 18 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line runs at 111% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 渋谷→表参道, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 1K ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. 1LDK ¥310,000 to ¥320,000 and 2LDK ¥500,000 to ¥510,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the highest in the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and a climb from the station to much of the housing holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Hanzomon is ahead on how close the centre is and lower rent.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hanzomon. Kojimachi has the Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line, a different set from Hanzomon. To Otemachi, for instance, Kojimachi takes 6 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥8,000 more at Kojimachi. On quiet, Hanzomon comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Ichigaya; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Hanzomon.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hanzomon. Ichigaya has 4 lines that Hanzomon does not. With more lines, Ichigaya is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Ichigaya is 9 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥31,000 less at Ichigaya. On how easy the shopping is, though, Hanzomon comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
notFor: People who would rather not walk up and down slopes
People who want another route when service is suspended
People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
新宿通り (3 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. Traffic on it never stops

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Neither the station nor the ground around it falls inside the projected flood area.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are very lightly loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
